correctness.rationale: Galuppi's monomial description gives weights \(1,1,2\) and all weighted-degree \(k\) monomials; for odd \(k=2r+1\) these exponent vectors project exactly to \(q,j\ge0\) with \(q+2j\le k\). Their convex hull has four primitive normal rays \((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-2),(0,-1)\), whose adjacent determinants are all one. The extra ray resolves the determinant-two cone of \(\mathbb P(1,1,2)\), with neighbor relation \((-1,-2)+(1,0)=2(0,-1)\), hence a \(-2\) exceptional curve. The base-point argument is exhaustive, and the normalized area agrees with the published degree formula. The packaged replay independently checks these combinatorial identities over many odd \(k\).

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural geometric question left visible by the published base-point and polygon calculations: what surface replaces \(\mathbb P(1,1,2)\) when odd weighted degree makes the parametrization indeterminate. It shows a sharp parity phenomenon and supplies the actual minimal resolution and polarization, useful for singularity, divisor, and intersection computations on this signature family.
